# Fixes: #[issue]

## Description

Adds mintsStrict (ms) field to PaymentRequest as specified in NUT-18 and NUT-26 pull request: https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/380.

When ms is absent or true (default), the recipient MUST reject payments from mints not in the mint list. When ms is false, the mint list is a suggestion for the payer only.

---

## Changes

- Add ms?: boolean to RawPaymentRequest type
- Add mintsStrict?: boolean to PaymentRequest constructor and all encode/decode paths (toRawRequest, toEncodedCreqB, fromRawRequest, fromEncodedRequest)
- Add TLV tag 0x09 (TAG_MINT_STRICT) to DecodedTLVPaymentRequest type and encode/decode logic in tlv.ts

---

- Was an issue opened prior to this PR? [No]
- Does this PR align with the current project direction and scope? [Yes]
- Link any relevant discussion or RFC: https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/380.

---

## Reviewer Notes

- Absence of ms is semantically equivalent to true (strict) — this matches the spec default and requires no migration of existing encoded requests
- mintsStrict is only serialized when explicitly set (!== undefined), so existing CBOR and TLV encodings are unchanged

---

labels.name: nut hold
labels.description: This PR is held pending the merge of a new or updated NUT

issue.body:
## Summary

Draft implementation of client-side primitives for the conditional token / prediction-market NUT proposal in https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/337.

This is intentionally opened as a draft because the NUT text is still under review and the API shape may need to change with maintainer feedback. The branch is based on current upstream `main` and excludes generated `lib/` output.

## What Is Included

- CTF condition-id and conditional-keyset helpers
- typed mint payloads/responses for conditional keyset discovery, condition registration, split/merge, and outcome redemption
- `Mint` methods for the proposed CTF endpoints
- optional `wallet.ctf` facade behind `new Wallet(mint, { enableCtf: true })`
- wallet/keychain validation that keeps conditional swaps within one conditional keyset and rejects mixed regular/conditional inputs
- node tests for CTF crypto helpers, mint payload handling, conditional keychain lookup, conditional swap, and redemption flows

## Review Notes

The implementation is meant to exercise the shape proposed in cashubtc/nuts#337 and provide concrete feedback from a TypeScript wallet implementation. In particular, it keeps conditional keysets out of regular NUT-02 keyset selection and treats condition-derived keysets as an explicit registry loaded through CTF endpoints.

This PR does not make CTF behavior default wallet behavior. Callers must opt into the facade with `enableCtf: true`.

Related reference implementation context from the NUT PR: https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/pull/1666

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npx vitest run --project node test/crypto/CTF.test.ts test/mint/Mint.node.test.ts test/wallet/keychain.node.test.ts test/wallet/wallet-ctf.node.test.ts`

comment.body:
Thanks for opening this as a draft. It's an interesting concept.

As requested, I’m treating this draft as a prototype/reference implementation, not something ready for full maintainer review.

Even if the NUT progresses to acceptance, there are a few high-level blockers before this could become reviewable - flagging now to make it easier for you later.

## Scope

This PR adds a large amount of public Mint/Wallet/KeyChain surface for a very niche application area.

Even with the `wallet.ctf` facade gated behind `enableCtf`, the PR still adds public `Wallet` methods, `Mint` methods, keyset metadata, and keychain behavior that every other consumer would have to carry.

Please keep CTF behind a much narrower experimental boundary, preferably without expanding core `Wallet`/`KeyChain` public surface.

See the `auth` module for the kind of encapsulation I mean.


## Compat overloads in Wallet

The compatibility overloads for the old v3-style methods are also unacceptable. We moved to the generic method-based APIs in v4, and overloading those same names to also behave like the old BOLT11 convenience methods is a step backwards.

It makes the API ambiguous, especially because `AmountLike` includes `string`, and it blurs the distinction between generic payment-method flows and the explicit first-class helpers like `createMintQuoteBolt11()` / `mintProofsBolt11()`.

Please remove the v3 compatibility overloads entirely.

## API

The public API needs looking at - the API Extractor report shows a bunch of forgotten exports and an explosion of changes in the public API.

## Docs & Tests

Finally, would need to add docs and complete test coverage when the API shape is intentional and stable enough to expose.

issue.title: refactor!: remove v4-deprecated APIs
issue.body:
## Summary

Removes the public symbols that were marked deprecated in v4.5.0, now that `main` is the v5 clean-break trunk:

- **`deriveSecret` / `deriveBlindingFactor`** (NUT-13) — replaced by `deriveSecretAndBlindingFactor`, which derives both values for a counter in one call.
- **`Wallet.completeMelt` boolean `preferAsync` overload** — callers pass `{ preferAsync: true }` on the `CompleteMeltOptions` object instead. The two overloads collapse back into a single signature.

issue.body:
Implements: https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/375

## Summary

Aligns the mint-quote signature messages with the amended cashubtc/nuts#375, which splits the two cases:

- **NUT-20** (single mint quote) is reverted to its original, retro-compatible message (`quote || B_0 || … || B_(n-1)`, plain hex concatenation). Wire format unchanged.
- **NUT-29** (batch mint) gets its own domain-separated, length-framed message in a new `src/crypto/NUT29.ts` (`signBatchMintQuote` / `verifyBatchMintQuoteSignature`):

  ```
  msg_to_sign = DST || len32(quote) || quote
                || for each output: len32(amount) || amount || len32(B_) || B_
  ```

  where `DST = "Cashu_MintQuoteSig_v1"`, `len32(x)` is the 4-byte big-endian length of `x`, `amount` is the canonical minimal big-endian encoding (`0` → empty), and `B_` is the raw compressed point. The signature is a BIP340 Schnorr signature over the SHA-256 of that byte string.

The batch-mint path (`prepareBatchMint`) now signs with `signBatchMintQuote`; the single-quote path is untouched. Tests are pinned to the canonical vector in `tests/29-tests.md` (`msg_hash = 03dc68d6…`).

## Motivation

The batch message now commits to each output's amount as well as its blinded point, in order, so a locked-quote signature cannot be replayed against a reordered or re-valued output set — this closes the output-malleability gap that the earlier separator-only approach left open. The length framing makes field boundaries unambiguous across curves (33-byte secp256k1 / 48-byte BLS points) without relying on point self-delimitation. NUT-20 keeps its existing format to avoid a needless break for already-deployed mints.

This changes the bytes signed for NUT-29 batch authentication; mints must adopt the same construction (per cashubtc/nuts#375) to verify.

issue.title: feat(mintinfo): add supportedMethods(op) to list usable mint/melt methods
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds a discovery convenience to `MintInfo`:

```ts
supportedMethods(op: 'mint' | 'melt'): SwapMethod[]   // [] when the op is disabled
```

Returns the method-unit settings the mint advertises for minting (NUT-04) or melting (NUT-05), so a consumer can enumerate what they can actually use (e.g. to build a method picker).

## Motivation

It's the discovery counterpart to the existing point-check `supportsMintMeltMethod(op, method, unit)`. Compared to the lower-level `isSupported(4 | 5).params`, it is:
- **operation-named** (no need to remember NUT-4 = mint, NUT-5 = melt), and
- **disabled-filtered** — `isSupported(4).params` returns methods even when the op is disabled; `supportedMethods` returns `[]`, so "supported" means *usable*.
